original_question: Does the quadratic lower bound lim inf_{T -> +infinity} log P(T) / log T >= 2 hold for every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism on a standard symplectic torus? More generally, does it hold on every aspherical closed symplectic manifold?
target_in_paper: Problem 2 in the contribution by Bernhard Albach, Umberto Hryniewicz, and Alexandru Oancea: the torus/aspherical-manifold test case of the broader quadratic-growth question for Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly targets the paper's narrower test case rather than the broader all-manifolds question: it asks for the quadratic lower bound itself, and it names exactly the two ambient classes appearing in Problem 2, namely standard symplectic tori and arbitrary aspherical closed symplectic manifolds. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
missing_details: P(T) is not defined. In the surrounding setup, for each T one counts periodic orbits with period at most T. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2602.12896))
The paper explicitly counts only primitive periodic orbits, excluding multiply covered orbits; your draft leaves this implicit. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2602.12896))

Because the object is a diffeomorphism, the stand-alone formulation should say that the period is the least positive integer period of a periodic orbit of the map; otherwise the T-parameter is underspecified. This is the discrete-time specialization of the paper's counting convention. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2602.12896))
The paper asks about periodic orbits, not periodic points; your draft should preserve that distinction. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

The torus should be identified explicitly as a standard symplectic torus, usually written (T^{2n}, omega_std), with arbitrary dimension; Problem 2 is not only about T^2. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))

For a fully stand-alone formulation, the second ambient class should be stated exactly as in the paper: an arbitrary aspherical closed symplectic manifold. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/html/2602.12896v1))
refined_question: Let varphi be a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of a standard symplectic torus (T^{2n}, omega_std), and for T>0 let P(T) denote the number of primitive periodic orbits of varphi whose least period is at most T (so multiply covered orbits are not counted). Must one have lim inf_{T -> +infinity} log P(T) / log T >= 2? More generally, does the same quadratic-growth lower bound hold for every Hamiltonian diffeomorphism of an arbitrary aspherical closed symplectic manifold? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2602.12896))
justification: The exact target in arXiv:2602.12896 is Problem 2, not the broader Problem 1. The nearby context first imports from Conjecture 1 the relevant counting convention—P(T) counts periodic orbits of period at most T and only primitive orbits are counted—and then presents Problem 2 as the torus/aspherical-manifold test case of the quadratic-growth question for Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms. The paragraph immediately after Problem 2 explains that the authors view this as a sharp lower-bound question motivated by low-dimensional integrable examples. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/2602.12896))
